memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Pharaoh said, "The Lord be with you—if I let you go, along with your women and children! Clearly you are bent on evil. No! Have only the men go and worship the Lord, since that's what you have been asking for." Then Moses and Aaron were driven out of Pharaoh's presence." - Exodus 10:10-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is Pharaoh's most cunning offer yet. Fine — the men can go and worship. Leave the children behind.

He knew exactly what he was doing. Keep the children, and the men will come back. Hold the next generation, and the whole nation stays in Egypt.

The strategy has never changed. There is enormous pressure on families today to let faith be a matter for adults while children are handed over to whatever shapes them — screens, schedules, sport, the noise of the culture. Parents are exhausted; church feels like one more thing; the children drift.

Do not accept this bargain. Moses would not, and neither should we.

Jesus was direct about children: let the little children come to me, and do not hinder them (Mk 10:14). He was rebuking His own disciples when He said it.

Whatever your household looks like, take the children with you when you go to worship. Their faith is not a later concern.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I taking the children in my life with me in matters of faith, or leaving them behind?
2. What is competing for the next generation's attention in my home?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I will not leave the children behind. Help me to lead them to You faithfully and patiently. Amen.
